query_text: Imagine that instead of presidential debates, we had rap battles. Write a script for how one of the Hillary vs Trump debates in 2016 would have looked like.

content.text:
**Title: “The 2016 Presidential Rap Battle”**  
*A fictional satirical script inspired by the Hillary Clinton vs. Donald Trump debates.*

---

### INT. DEBATE STAGE — NIGHT

A huge debate hall. Red, white, and blue lights flash like a boxing arena. Instead of podiums, there are two microphones on stands. A DJ sits behind a table labeled **“DJ DEMOCRACY.”**

The moderator, **LESTER**, steps forward in a suit, holding cue cards.

**LESTER:**  
Good evening, America. Tonight’s presidential debate will follow a slightly different format. Each candidate will have ninety seconds to answer the question — in rhyme.

Crowd cheers.

**LESTER:**  
Secretary Clinton. Mr. Trump. Welcome to the first presidential rap battle.

**DJ DEMOCRACY:**  
Yo, candidates ready?

**HILLARY:**  
Ready.

**TRUMP:**  
I was born ready. Very ready. The readiest.

**LESTER:**  
First topic: the economy.

DJ drops a beat.

---

## ROUND ONE: THE ECONOMY

### HILLARY steps to the mic.

**HILLARY:**  
I’ve been in the room where the hard choices happen,  
While you were on TV doing boardroom cappin’.  
You say you’re a builder, you say you’re elite,  
But your plans got more holes than your bankrupt receipts.  

You talk big numbers, all flash, no facts,  
Like, “Trust me, folks,” then dodge the tax.  
I’ve got policy papers, binders stacked high,  
You’ve got hand gestures and a spray-tanned sky.  

I’m talking jobs, wages, college tuition,  
You’re tweeting at dawn with no clear position.  
You say you’re a winner, but here’s the reveal:  
America needs plans, not another bad deal.

Crowd: “Ooooooh!”

**LESTER:**  
Mr. Trump, your response.

### TRUMP adjusts his tie, steps forward.

**TRUMP:**  
Crooked Hillary, let me be totally clear,  
You’ve been in Washington thirty long years.  
You had your chance, now you want one more?  
But the people are tired of the same old chore.  

I built towers, hotels, big golden doors,  
You built committees and endless reports.  
You say you’ve got binders, well that’s very neat,  
But I made my name on Fifth Avenue street.  

You talk about plans, but nobody reads ’em,  
I talk to the workers, I’m saying I’ll lead ’em.  
Jobs went overseas, politicians got paid,  
I’ll bring them all back with the best trade deals made.  

Believe me, believe me, I’m winning this fight,  
Your whole campaign needs an email rewrite.

Crowd explodes.

**HILLARY:**  
That was cute.

**TRUMP:**  
It was tremendous.

---

## ROUND TWO: FOREIGN POLICY

**LESTER:**  
Next question: How would you handle foreign policy?

Beat changes. More dramatic.

### TRUMP goes first.

**TRUMP:**  
The world’s laughing at us, I hear it all day,  
Bad deals, weak leaders, giving power away.  
I’ll walk in the room and they’ll know who I am,  
A negotiator with a tremendous plan.  

NATO? They’re paying. Trade? I’ll review it.  
Bad deal on the table? I’ll walk right through it.  
You voted for wars, you backed interventions,  
Now you want lectures on global intentions?  

You call me unstable, but here’s what’s bizarre:  
You lost your emails, now you want the czar?  
The world needs strength, not another reset,  
I’m the boss-level threat they haven’t seen yet.

Crowd murmurs, some cheers, some boos.

**LESTER:**  
Secretary Clinton.

### HILLARY steps up, calm and deliberate.

**HILLARY:**  
Foreign policy isn’t a branding event,  
It’s knowing what every decision has meant.  
You don’t run the world like a reality show,  
With a catchphrase prepared and no place to go.  

I sat with allies, I studied the stakes,  
I know what a reckless statement can break.  
You praise strongmen, then call it “strategy,”  
But chaos and ego are not diplomacy.  

You say “believe me” when the facts disappear,  
I say read a briefing, then come back here.  
Commander-in-chief takes judgment and skill,  
Not late-night tweets and an impulse thrill.  

You want the nuclear codes? Here’s my objection:  
You can’t even handle your own comment section.

Crowd: “OOOOOOH!”

**TRUMP:**  
Wrong. Very wrong.

**HILLARY:**  
Check the transcript.

---

## ROUND THREE: CHARACTER

**LESTER:**  
The next topic is character and temperament.

The beat becomes darker, heavier.

### HILLARY takes the mic.

**HILLARY:**  
You built a campaign on insult and fear,  
Pointing at everyone, year after year.  
Women, immigrants, anyone in your lane,  
You turn public service into personal pain.  

You say you’re tough, but you’re thin as a thread,  
Someone tweets once and you’re out of bed.  
A president can’t be baited with ease,  
By comedy sketches or magazine leads.  

I’ve taken the hits, the hearings, the heat,  
Stood through the pressure, stayed on my feet.  
You call me nasty? Fine, here’s the claim:  
If competence is nasty, remember the name.

Crowd cheers loudly.

**LESTER:**  
Mr. Trump.

### TRUMP grins and walks slowly to center stage.

**TRUMP:**  
You talk about character, that’s quite a scene,  
With scandals behind you like a limousine.  
You say you’re prepared, but prepared for what?  
More speeches to banks while the factories shut?  

You play the victim, you play the pro,  
But everybody watching already knows:  
Same old system, same old crew,  
Same old promises that never come true.  

I’m not politically polished, it’s true,  
But that’s why the crowd says, “He’s not like you.”  
I broke the machine, I changed the game,  
You spent your whole life protecting the same.  

Call me thin-skinned, call me uncouth,  
But I’m saying what millions think is the truth.  
You’re the past with a résumé laminated,  
I’m the future — gold-plated.

Crowd mixed: cheers and boos.

**HILLARY:**  
Gold-plated is not the same as qualified.

**TRUMP:**  
It is if it’s very high quality.

---

## ROUND FOUR: EMAILS VS. TAXES

**LESTER:**  
We now move to specific controversies. Secretary Clinton, your emails. Mr. Trump, your taxes.

Beat gets faster.

### TRUMP jumps in.

**TRUMP:**  
Emails deleted, servers in closets,  
Every explanation makes voters nauseous.  
Thirty thousand gone, what a magic trick,  
Now you want trust? That’s a hard sell, quick.  

You say it was careless, not meant to deceive,  
But why should the people continue to believe?  
If I did that, they’d lock me away,  
But Clinton rules mean a different play.  

I’m audited, I’m smart, I use the code,  
You’ve been in office while the loopholes growed—  
Grew. Whatever. The point is clear:  
You had the power and left them here.

Crowd laughs.

**HILLARY smirks.**

**HILLARY:**  
You corrected your grammar. I’m proud.

### HILLARY takes the mic.

**HILLARY:**  
Yes, I made mistakes, and I’ve said that before,  
But let’s talk taxes — open that door.  
You hide your returns like they’re state secrets too,  
What’s in those papers you don’t want in view?  

Maybe you’re not as rich as you claim,  
Maybe your charities don’t match the name,  
Maybe your debts have a curious source,  
Maybe your “genius” is just losing with force.  

You bragged that not paying was making you smart,  
But schools, roads, troops — taxes play a part.  
So before you call others corrupt or lax,  
Show us the receipts. Release the tax.

Crowd chants: “Release the tax! Release the tax!”

**TRUMP:**  
I will release them when the audit is finished.

**HILLARY:**  
That beat has been looping for months.

---

## FINAL ROUND: CLOSING STATEMENTS

**LESTER:**  
Candidates, final bars. Why should America choose you?

Beat softens, then builds.

### HILLARY steps forward.

**HILLARY:**  
This country is bigger than one man’s name,  
Bigger than rallies, slogans, fame.  
It’s families working, students in debt,  
Veterans waiting for promises met.  

It’s daughters watching what leaders allow,  
It’s sons asking what courage means now.  
I’m not perfect, I won’t claim to be,  
But I’ve spent my life in service, visibly.  

You may not love every choice I’ve made,  
But I know the weight when decisions are weighed.  
So if you want steady, if you want prepared,  
If you want someone who’s been there and cared —  
Vote for the future, not fear in disguise.  
America’s promise is how we rise.

Crowd applauds.

**LESTER:**  
Mr. Trump.

### TRUMP walks to the front, crowd energy shifts.

**TRUMP:**  
America’s tired of polished lines,  
Tired of waiting in government lines.  
Tired of leaders who promise and stall,  
Tired of experts who don’t fix it at all.  

I’m not from the script, I’m not from the mold,  
I say what I mean, sometimes too bold.  
But people feel forgotten, mocked, ignored,  
I kicked down the gate, now they’re through the door.  

You can call it chaos, call it noise,  
But millions out there finally have a voice.  
I’ll cut bad deals, build strength, bring pride,  
Put America first and turn the tide.  

So if you want change, not another rerun,  
Vote Trump 2016 — we’ve only begun.

Crowd erupts.

---

### The beat cuts.

**LESTER:**  
Thank you, candidates. That concludes tonight’s presidential rap battle.

**DJ DEMOCRACY:**  
No matter who you support, please vote.

Hillary and Trump awkwardly stand near each other.

**HILLARY:**  
Handshake?

**TRUMP:**  
We’ll see. Depends on the ratings.

**LESTER:**  
Good night, America.

Lights fade as the crowd chants:

**CROWD:**  
Vote! Vote! Vote! Vote!

**END.**
